newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's negotiator appears at site to meet rebel.
newsitem.headline: Peru's negotiator appears at site to meet rebel.

text.p: The Peruvian government's negotiator Domingo Palermo arrived on Tuesday at the site of the besieged Japanese ambassador's home for peace talks with a spokesman for Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages, witnesses said.
Palermo appeared in the police security zone around the residence about 2:55 p.m (1955 GMT).

The long-awaited meeting was set to take place in a two- floor terracotta-coloured building across the street from the diplomatic mansion. The Red Cross, overseeing the talks, erected a big Red Cross flag on the roof.
Palermo was due to meet the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) second-in-command, Rolly Rojas, according to the government.

Before Palermo appeared at the site, Red Cross official Michel Minnig and Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent -- members of a commission for the talks -- arrived with Terusuke Tarada, the Japanese government's observer.
The Vatican's representative on the commission, Peruvian Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, arrived minutes after Palermo.
The commission and negotiator then walked together into the building where they waited for Rojas.
Special police force officers in neighbouring houses watched while sharpshooters on nearby roofs kept their rifles trained on the building.

Police also tightened security in the area. They pushed hordes of journalists behind security lines to a distance of three blocks from the residence and restricted access to the zone with vehicle and dog patrols.
President Alberto Fujimori said he hoped the meeting -- the first direct talks between the apparently intransigent sides since Dec. 28, 1996, -- would pave the way for an end to the crisis.

"Now these conversations are beginning, I would say that there are elements that give us a certain optimism," Fujimori told Peruvian reporters Tuesday in London. "(Rojas) is a sociologist familiar with the theme and he could help us find a solution."
